note: Lalit uses both Ma, so it cannot belong to Marwa thaat, which has only tivra Ma. Wikipedia and Tanarang both classify it as Poorvi.
Tanarang gives the 4th prahar of the night, 3-6am, which straddles prahar 8 (1-4am) and prahar 1 (4-7am). The dataset's 1 is defensible for a pre-dawn raga; no change recommended.
Pa is generally skipped in the ascent; Tanarang says so in prose while its own table prints P. Pa remains in the avaroha and the pakad. Some gharanas keep it, hence medium rather than high.
Dha is vadi and Ga samvadi; the dataset has the pair reversed. Confirmed by the article infobox, body text, pakad emphasis, and Kanada-group teaching.
Companion to the vadi fix. The pair must be swapped together.
Shuddha Asavari is audava in ascent (Ga and Ni varjya) and sampurna in descent. The dataset's seven-note ascent describes a different raga.
Sources give a vakra descent, S' n d P m P d m P g R S. The dataset's plain line is recognisable but drops the m P d m P turn. No forced replacement without a musical decision.
Source ascents begin on lower Ni ('n S g M P n S'). The dataset notation has no prefix-octave marker, so the pickup cannot be written. Notation limit, not a musical error.
Multani is a noon raga, 12-3pm, which is prahar 4 (13:00-16:00), not 5. Both sources agree on 12-3.
Source ascent begins on lower Ni ('N S g M P N S'). Notation cannot express the pickup. Separately, both sites' prose wrongly calls the Madhyam tivra; their notation uses shuddha Ma.

Three published pairs: Sa-Pa (Tanarang and most teaching sites), Re-Pa (Bor via Wikipedia), Ga-Ni (the dataset). At least one teacher explicitly rejects Ga-Ni because it pulls the raga towards Shankara. Undecided; null is safer than another contested swap.
Companion to the vadi question. Pa is the constant in all the mainstream pairings, but the vadi is not settled, so the pair cannot be fixed.
Tanarang gives the 2nd prahar of the night, 9pm-12am, which maps to prahar 7 (22:00-01:00). Evening-opening practice supports 6, hence medium.
Sources give a vakra descent, S' (n)d n P M P (M)g M R S. The dataset has S' n P d M P g M R S, losing the n-P cadence that identifies the raga. Plausible variant; undecided.
Ma is the common choice and Tanarang's; Wikipedia lists Ma/Pa as disputed. The dataset follows the mainstream reading; recorded as contested, not as an error.

Tanarang gives 1st prahar of the day (6-9am) or sarvakalik (any time); the raga is also the standard concert closer. Prahar 2 (7-10am) sits inside the morning window, so no change, but the field is inherently soft.
The source contradicts itself: infobox 12-3am (prahar 8), body text 9pm-12am (prahar 7). The dataset matches the body text. No change recommended.
Ma vadi, Sa samvadi in Wikipedia, Tanarang and Sangeetapriya. One tutorial gives Dha, which is the outlier.
Companion to the vadi fill.
Durga is a second-prahar-of-night raga, 9pm-12am, i.e. prahar 7 (22:00-01:00).
Tanarang gives Pancham vadi, Shadj samvadi. The dataset's Ma vadi is a common simplification but not the standard assignment.
The raga uses both Nishads (Tanarang: 'Both Nishads'); the dataset has no shuddha Ni anywhere. Suggested array is a linear approximation of a vakra ascent.

Shuddha Ni is missing from the descent. Tanarang says Dha is varjya in avaroh but its own notation includes D, so the source is internally inconsistent; the suggested line keeps D and adds the n-P turn.
Source ascent begins on lower Ni (N S R M P N S'). The notation cannot express a prefix-octave pickup. Notation limit, not a musical error.
Both sources give Ga vadi and Ni samvadi. Low confidence only because Pilu is light-classical and treated as time- and grammar-flexible.
Companion to the vadi fill.
Wikipedia and Tanarang give the third part of the day, 12-3pm (prahar 4). Chandrakantha lists Pilu as 'any time'. The dataset's 6 is defensible for an evening thumri; needs a product decision.
Pilu uses both Ga, both Dha and both Ni; the single-line Kafi ascent hides all three alternations. No single linear array is correct.
Majority reading is Sa vadi, Pa samvadi. Pa-Sa and Ga-Dha are also published. There is no Wikipedia raga article (Pahadi redirects to a disambiguation page), so the field is genuinely unsettled.
Companion to the vadi fill; same uncertainty.
The source contradicts itself: infobox gives Dha/Re, body text gives Ma/Sa. The dataset follows the body text, which is also the common teaching. Recorded, not corrected.
Companion to the vadi question.
Bhatkhande places Malkauns in Bhairavi thaat; some sources say Asavari. Bhairavi is the common choice and the dataset's value is fine. Recorded as a variant.
